transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Cho (Redwood SE), Lena Rodriguez (Head of ML, PhoenixAI), Tom Nguyen (Infra Lead), Raj Patel (CTO)

Summary: quick discovery call around migrating from OpenAI-hosted endpoints to Redwood Dedicated. Focus on compatibility (vLLM/TGI parity), eval parity, latency/cost tradeoffs, and security/VPC requirements.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. I'm Maya, AE on the Redwood side, and with me is Ethan our SE. Quick round - can you tell us what you're hoping to get out of the call?
[00:08] Lena: Hi, yeah thanks. I'm Lena, head of ML at PhoenixAI. We're evaluating moving some traffic off OpenAI to reduce costs and have more control. Main asks: throughput predictability, latency stays similar for our 512 token chats, and eval parity - outputs must match or be within tolerance.
[00:23] Tom: And I'm Tom on infra - we need to understand network/VPC options, SSO, kms, and audit logs. Also curious about whether we need to run vLLM in-house or Redwood Dedicated handles it.
[00:34] Ethan: Great - thanks. Quick question on your current setup: are you using gpt-4o or mixed models? and are you using streaming?
[00:42] Raj: We're mostly on gpt-4o for core chat, some gpt-4. We do streaming and have a batch embedding pipeline on side. Latency SLO is 300ms p50 for short prompts and up to 1s p50 for 512 tokens; p95 targets are looser but we'd like under 1.2s.
[01:00] Maya: ok good. And volume? rough rps?
[01:03] Lena: Peak is ~40rps, average 12rps, with bursts to 60 during heavy churn.
[01:10] Ethan: That's exactly the kind of workload Redwood Dedicated is tuned for - reserved capacity to hit predictable throughput. A few clarifying items: do you need data residency or on-prem?
[01:20] Tom: We need EU residency for a subset of customers, and for some regulated customers we might need a VPC or on-prem option.
[01:28] Maya: We can support that - Dedicated can be provisioned in region and Private/VPC is an option for the regulated set. We'll share the Private onboarding doc.
[01:35] Lena: One big technical thing - our stack uses vLLM in front of TGI for some models; will Redwood Dedicated accept the same model artifacts, and will behavior line up?
[01:45] Ethan: short answer: in most cases yes, but there are caveats. We support common model formats and quantized variants; runtime differences (kv cache, attention kernels) can lead to small output deltas. We do model onboarding and eval parity testing as part of the migration.
[02:00] Tom: Can you be more specific about the most common parity gaps?
[02:05] Ethan: Sure. Two common sources: different tokenizer versions or byte-pair merges, and model weight conversion quirks when switching quantizers (8-bit vs 4-bit). Also runtime decoding differences - e.g., beam/search seeding and sampling RNG - can change outputs slightly.
[02:20] Lena: We need deterministic or at least consistent outputs for a set of customer-critical prompts. How do you measure parity?
[02:27] Maya: We'll run a side-by-side eval: we take your prompt set and run on OpenAI/current prod and on Dedicated candidate, then compute metrics - exact match where applicable, kernel-level embedding cosine similarity, and human-judged rating for quality.
[02:40] Raj: How do you handle prompt-engineering differences? sometimes we seed with system-level context and rely on their llm-specific behavior.
[02:47] Ethan: We'll include system prompts in the eval. Also we have a 'quality-monitor' pipeline to watch regressions over time tied to specific prompt sets. If parity gaps are unacceptable, we can try different quantization profiles or fall back to a larger float model.
[03:05] Tom: What's the deployment model? is this fully managed on Redwood infra or do we get a VPC with customer-managed nodes?
[03:11] Maya: Dedicated is Redwood-managed but single-tenant - you get reserved GPU pools and network isolation. Private/VPC gives you dedicated control plane and network peering; on-prem is available for strict air-gapped needs.
[03:25] Tom: For Private/VPC do you integrate with our KMS? we need CMKs for encryption at rest.
[03:30] Ethan: Yes, we have KMS integrations (AWS KMS, Google KMS, HSM via partners). We'll capture key rotation and audit log details in the security doc.
[03:40] Lena: Pricing - can you ballpark Dedicated vs Hosted?
[03:44] Maya: Ballpark, Dedicated is committed capacity with lower per-token cost but capex-like commitment. Hosted is pay-as-you-go higher unit price. We'll send the pricing sheet; it includes examples for your 40rps workload with batching configs.
[03:56] Raj: Batch size / batching behavior is important - sometimes we batch to save cost but that increases tail latency. Can Redwood guarantee low tail latency with batching?
[04:05] Ethan: We have workload-aware batching; you can set latency SLOs and the runtime adapts. Continuous KV caching and prefix caching reduce token work for repeated prefixes. For strict tail-latency SLOs we partition capacity for low-latency routes.
[04:20] Lena: You mentioned kernel selection earlier - will you choose int8 kernels automatically? we have many short chats so quantization helps.
[04:28] Ethan: Kernel selection is automatic but we surface recommended quantization profiles per model. For short chat where quality is sensitive we often recommend int8 or mixed-precision instead of aggressive 4-bit.
[04:38] Tom: About compatibility with TGI - we have some custom TGI endpoints and wrappers. Does Redwood support TGI-like api or do we need to refactor?
[04:48] Ethan: We can support either - Redwood's API is compatible with common inference patterns (streaming, function calling). For bespoke TGI wrappers we usually adapt via a thin shim during onboarding.
[04:57] Lena: What's the timeline to run a pilot? we'd like to do a 2-week POC that's representative of production with traffic replay.
[05:03] Maya: Totally doable. Typical pilot plan: 1) share eval prompts and samples, 2) Redwood runs bench parity and shares results, 3) we provision a small Dedicated pool for pilot, 4) traffic replay and monitoring + joint baseline comparison. Usually 3-4 weeks to get meaningful results.
[05:20] Raj: Security questions we'll want answered: SOC 2 Type II, ISO, SSO (SAML/OIDC), RBAC, audit logs retention, and data deletion guarantees.
[05:30] Maya: We'll send the security pack - it covers SOC2, ISO27001, SAML, RBAC, audit logs, and data handling policies. For Private, we can give more control over logs and retention.
[05:40] Tom: For evaluation stats we also need token accounting parity - different runtimes sometimes count tokens differently which affects costs.
[05:47] Ethan: We'll include tokenization parity checks in the benchmark - same tokenizer/detokenizer pipeline is used. If there's divergence, we flag it and suggest a mapping.
[05:58] Lena: Any gotchas with streaming and function calling when moving from OpenAI? We rely on function-calling heavily in product.
[06:05] Ethan: We support function/tool calling. Main gotcha is how partial outputs are flushed during streaming - small differences can exist. We'll exercise your function-calling flows during the pilot.
[06:17] Speaker 5: (inaudible)
[06:20] Maya: lol noted.
[06:22] Lena: Ok, walk me through a concrete benchmark plan - what do you need from us and what do you run?
[06:28] Ethan: We'll need: (1) a canonical set of ~100-300 prompts for quality eval, (2) a replay set of traffic (anonymized logs) for perf testing, (3) the model specs and any custom tokenizers. We'll run side-by-side tests: latency distribution, token cost per request, output diff metrics, embedding cos sims for embedding workloads, and human eval on a sample. We'll produce a report with recommendations: batching, quant profiles, and any model swaps.
[06:55] Raj: If parity fails, is fallback to hosted Redwood or OpenAI supported? we need graceful degradation.
[07:02] Maya: Yes, we support routing policies and automatic fallbacks to hosted endpoints or alternate model variants.
[07:08] Tom: Are there any networking prerequisites for Dedicated? VPN? peering?
[07:12] Ethan: Typically we do VPC peering or private link for EU deployments; for Dedicated we manage the infra but allow secure peering to your VPC. For Private we do customer-managed nodes in your network.
[07:25] Lena: Ok great. Anything around regulatory/compliance for healthcare customers? we have a subset handling PHI and need HIPAA assurances.
[07:33] Maya: We have HIPAA controls in Private and Dedicated with BAAs available. We'll include that in the security pack.
[07:40] Tom: Let's talk numbers briefly - can you hypothetically show cost delta? simple example: 1M tokens/month.
[07:46] Maya: We'll put numbers in the pricing sheet but high-level: Hosted might be X cents/token; Dedicated with commitment can be 30-50% lower depending on utilization and batching. We'll model your workload in the sheet.
[07:58] Lena: For the pilot we want to measure both cost and latency; also check hallucination regressions.
[08:05] Ethan: we'll add hallucination checks into the human evaluation and automated checks where possible (e.g., fact-check heuristics).
[08:12] Raj: Ok, next steps?
[08:15] Maya: I'll send pricing and security docs. Ethan will send a benchmark plan and list of inputs required. Lena will share the prompt set and sample logs. We'll target a pilot kickoff in two weeks - propose dates in the next email.
[08:28] Lena: Sounds good.
[08:30] Maya: Any final questions?
[08:32] Tom: One last thing - what's the typical SLA and uptime for Dedicated?
[08:36] Maya: Dedicated has an SLA backed by reserved capacity - 99.9% uptime is typical for enterprise contracts; exact terms depend on the contract.
[08:45] Raj: Perfect. Thanks everyone.
[08:48] Maya: Thanks, we'll follow up with materials.

Action items (in-call):
- Maya to share pricing and security pack.
- Ethan to draft benchmark plan and requirements.
- Lena to share eval prompts and anonymized logs.
- Tom to confirm VPC/on-prem preference.

References shared: Redwood Dedicated overview deck (link in chat: https://redwood.example/decks/dedicated-overview), Security pack (link: https://redwood.example/security-pack), Example benchmark template (link: https://redwood.example/benchmarks/template).

End of transcript.
